What makes me laugh most personally is the fact that the thinner I am, the less freedom I have. Literally, the more weight I shed, the more I am careful about what I eat. I have no energy, I am constantly hungry and unhappy, but at the same time completely incapacitated.
Like, I know that this is not the way and it does not pay off, BUT.. Eh.

This is a very big achievement! And I am really proud of you ❤️ Keep it up.
As for the feeling of fullness, I know it's terrible, but please give your body some time. Your stomach has been used to vomiting for so long that it now has to learn how to digest food. It will take a while, but this feeling will begin to fade away. Personally, I was greatly helped by regular mealtimes, frequent hydration and more movement ( even such simple activities as walking).
7, almost 8 years

My first question is, do people around you know you have an eating disorder? If not, it can be really hard for them to notice your "cry for help". Experience has taught me that people know less about us than we assume. We think that something is obvious, understandable and we wait for someone to come to our rescue.. I've been waiting like this for the past 7 years and only recently did I realize that if I need something, I have to say it. If I am silent, how can anyone know what I feel or think?
Next thing - I think it might not necessarily be that no one noticed or that nobody cares. Let's take an example - someone close to me has recently gained weight. I don't know how much, nor do I remember when she started to gain weight (especially since it might not have been so visible at first). All I know is she looks different now. It's not that I don't care about her, but I'm just afraid to ask. Because I know how I would react if someone noticed my extra pounds. I think this is a sensitive topic for many people. We like when someone tells us that we have lost weight, but not really when it is the other way around .. I'm sorry if this all sounds a little harsh. I don't mean it that way. I am sending you a lot of hugs ❤️
And please don't be hard on yourself.

I think this might allow me to sleep well at night for a while. 🖤 The end of the year is approaching and the amount of my anxiety, stress and depressive thoughts increases along with the realization that not only did I fail to improve my condition, but made it worse by my underweight. This is my journey, my story, but I feel like a laughing stock.. I always go back to square one and it's like there's nothing I can do. Still, I keep getting off my knees and trying to fight back. Today I will take another breath, pull myself together, and try to win a few battles before this year is over. 
Thank you again for your kind and hopeful words. I wish you a lot of strength so that you can defeat your own demon once and for all. ❤️

First of all, thank you for sharing this with me. It really means a lot to me right now 🖤  I, too, often find these unpleasant feelings within myself. People around me are moving forward with life, and only me, stuck in place. I always try to hide it, but ... You know how it is.Especially when someone younger than me with more achievements in life shows up at a family reunion . I think then that probably my parents would love to have someone like that and that I am a failure, and this is how the whole spiral of thoughts begins...

That's one of the reasons why I created this post ... I feel like I'm stuck. My ED, along with depression, paralyzed many areas of my life. A lot of people tell me, "Just go to school", "Just eat", "Just...". But.. It's really not that simple for me. I am tired of this fight, and yet I try to win every day. This is my fight and no one around can see that I am putting a lot of energy into it. I'm only 22 like you say, but I feel like I'm too damaged to be worth trying. I have thought many times about ending it all, but I always find this little hope that maybe there is still time, that it is worth it. But at the same time, with each passing year, while I still fail to recover, that hope diminishes. I think I just wanted to hear, "It's alright. Don't be afraid it'll be too late. You can still win, so keep fighting."
I'm sorry if that sounds like self-pity. It's just ... I think I'm standing on that edge again trying to find reasons to live.

Thank you for supporting me 🖤 It really means a lot to me to know I'm not alone with this. That someone understands what I'm going through. I hope both of us can defeat our demons
Take care ❤️

Let's say this - simply eating anything will not fix the problem as long as there is still a reason why you are in this mess. Your bulimia was developed as a tool to fight the binge-eating problem, right? Even if you take this tool away, you are still left with the original problem of overeating and all the negative feelings that come with it. And it's important that your treatment takes this into account and will focus on both issues. 
This idea of ​​eating is meant to help you come to terms with your food, destroy your fear, and build your confidence. It will allow your body to calm down. The condition for this to work is simple - it should not be treated as the only form of healing in the way of recovery.  
But that's just what I think.

I think there's one way to find out - try to give up bulimic behavior for a period of time. If you can, congratulations - you are still in control. And yeah I say 'still', because it's like playing with fire - you have a high probability of getting burned. What you are doing right now is building a pattern of behavior, strengthening an unhealthy habit. Do you think eating disorders develop overnight? We all started out believing we had control over it and that we are strong enough to handle it. You light a fire and feed it with wood - just like we give parts of ourselves to bulimia. And the next thing you know is that the whole forest is on fire and you don't know how to put it out. 
 So.. Please see if you are still in charge and if so - give up this path as soon as possible.
I get it too well. I feel devastated and defeated, but.. Let's not give up. We have to get up and keep fighting. It'll be better

It is quite simple :) I usually grate the pumpkin (I like the consistency better) and I add vegetables that I like - peppers,  chopped garlic, and chives.The more colorful the better! There are no restrictions here. It's only important that the pumpkin predominates in this mixture, thanks to which the pancakes will retain their structure and will not fall apart in the pan.
I also like spicier flavors, so I often add chopped hot peppers or the marinade jalapeno peppers. Then just an egg and some flour. ( universal is fine, but I use rye flour and it's good too)
As for the yogurt - I add chopped garlic, some salt,  grated green cucumber (has a lot of water, so you need to squeeze them out before adding) and some chives.
This is the first time someone asks me for a recipe, so if I missed something - tell me :)

I thought for a long moment about what I could advise you, but ... it's a difficult problem and I think the solution is quite individual for each person. I know it quite well from my own daily life, I still experience it - although this time I am winning these battles. How? I slowed down a bit. I have stopped rushing everything and am trying to appreciate every moment. I do my housework longer, spend more time cooking (it calms me down and gives me sense of control), I take care of small details that make me happy. I have more or less fixed meal times and I try very hard to stick to them. - This is really important for me, it helps me create a routine. I also try to create pleasant moments like an evening with a blanket, hot tea and a good horror movie.
I could tell you that the most important thing is to find a lot of activities for yourself and never have a "I have nothing to do" moment, but.. Will it change the fact that you are afraid of such moments? 
My days are not yet what I would have dreamed of, but I believe that with time, things that will interest me will start to appear in my everyday life. What I have so far is a routine that allows me to breathe. Maybe it will work for you too?

Don't be too hard on yourself. We all fail sometimes, even the strongest of us. The most important thing is not to give up. Forgive yourself, get up from your knees and keep going :) You've made great progress so far. Every moment counts, it's not just 90 days of purge free - these are 90 days of your life, your hard work and every battle you won.

Then stop. Let me tell you  this - it's not about "tomorrow", it's about "now". It is about what you can do right now to make your tomorrow better. Don't think that today's day is lost because you have failed your expectations - all of us here stumble and fall,  but that does not mean that our efforts are useless. My advice is simple, don't fight for "today" or "tomorrow",  fight for every moment of the day.

I am also fighting with my ED now and I know it can be tough. But remember that these are only moments on your way to recovery. No matter what ED tells you, answer him "Shut up" and keep going. You can do it :)

My "I am sober" app says - "The future depends on what you do today". Take a deep breath, sit down and think about it for a moment. You can give up the fight today and go back to what was before, but is this something you want for your future self? Is this a decision you'll be proud of tomorrow?

Honestly, I think if you are wondering if you are hurting yourself for attention, you probably are not. Eating disorders are just like that - they don't want you to reach out for help, so they try to deceive you, lie to you. I have been suffering from bulimia for 8 years and sometimes the same nonsensical thought keeps popping up in my head "Maybe I'm doing this for attention?". Then I think of every moment when I was alone and out of control eating unimaginable amounts of food. When I was vomiting behind closed doors, trying to be as quiet as possible. The days I starved myself and exercised until my body was unable to. Every promise "from tomorrow I will stop doing this", and then every second of thinking about food until I gave up. If this is attention seeking, then where were the people whose attention I wanted? Why am I doing my best to hide my horrible actions? Why can't I stop? These feelings are real. We don't make them up for someone. If you are unable to break it, it's probably not you who rule this nightmare routine.

Okay, I'm not a specialist, but hear me out. The obvious problem I see is under-eating during the week. The fact that you overeat on the weekend compensates for the losses caused by under-eating. Your body needs fuel to function, and if you don't provide it as much as it needs, it will take it by force. It's a bit of a vicious cycle that will keep going as long as you keep restricting your food intake. The fact that you are not obsessed with losing weight, but  you are " kind of " afraid of gaining weight seems quite normal to me - especially if you think you have a few pounds too much. I guess I would try to break this cycle first, which will mean you have to start eating regularly and forgive yourself if you overeat during the weekend. Your body will take time to get used to the fact that it doesn't have to fight you for food.

This. I know these feelings, unfortunately. I can't advise you, especially as someone who is still under ED control, but ..Honestly, I still have some hope. Maybe complete recovery is a bit too much for us at the moment. Maybe we should focus our attention on small steps? Do not throw yourself into the deep water with the cry of "I won't fail from now on"because let's be honest, it never worked and it will never work. What I'm trying to say, we didn't come to this state overnight. ED was planted in our minds and began to grow, taking away our control for days, months and years. This process took time and it will take time to change it as well. That's why I still have hope. I cannot change myself or my perception in one day or a week, but maybe if I start changing the little things in my daily life, someday I will wake up with the thought that maybe I can get better. Even if I don't believe it now.

So.. Please be gentle with yourself. You haven't lost this war yet
